mcqs.learning_point: Understand the basic idea of pressure
mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines pressure?

options.A: Pressure is the force applied per unit area.
options.B: Pressure is the total force acting on an object.
options.C: Pressure is the mass of an object divided by its volume.
options.D: Pressure is the speed of an object multiplied by its mass.

mcqs.answer: Pressure is the force applied per unit area.
mcqs.explanation: Pressure is defined as the amount of force acting on a surface per unit area (P = F/A). It is different from force, which is just the push or pull itself, and from density (mass/volume) or momentum (mass × velocity). Option A states the correct definition; the other options describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate pressure to force and area
mcqs.question: A student presses a book with a force of 20 N over an area of 0.04 m². What is the pressure exerted on the book?
mcqs.explanation: Pressure (P) is calculated using P = F / A. Substituting the given values: P = 20 N / 0.04 m² = 500 N/m² = 500 Pa. Option C matches this result; the other options are the result of incorrect division or misplaced decimal places.

mcqs.learning_point: Explain why sharp objects exert greater pressure
mcqs.question: Why does a nail pierce wood more easily than a blunt screwdriver when the same force is applied?

options.A: Because the nail is made of stronger metal.
options.B: Because the nail has a smaller contact area, producing greater pressure.
options.C: Because the nail is sharper, which reduces the force needed.
options.D: Because wood offers less resistance to pointed objects.

mcqs.answer: Because the nail has a smaller contact area, producing greater pressure.
mcqs.explanation: Pressure equals force divided by area. A sharp nail has a very small tip area, so the same applied force results in a much higher pressure, allowing it to cut through wood. Option B directly states this principle. Options A and D refer to material strength or wood resistance, which are not the primary reason. Option C mixes the idea of sharpness with force reduction, which is misleading.

mcqs.question: A diver is at a depth of 10 meters underwater. The total pressure at that depth is about 2 atmospheres (including atmospheric pressure). If atmospheric pressure at sea level is 1 atm, what is the pressure due to the water alone?
mcqs.explanation: Total pressure = atmospheric pressure + water pressure. Given total = 2 atm and atmospheric = 1 atm, water pressure = 2 atm – 1 atm = 1 atm. Option B is correct; the other options either underestimate or overestimate the water’s contribution.

mcqs.question: Which statement about atmospheric pressure is correct?

options.A: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air above us per unit area.
options.B: Atmospheric pressure is the same as the pressure inside a tire.
options.C: Atmospheric pressure only exists at sea level.
options.D: Atmospheric pressure is measured in meters.

mcqs.answer: Atmospheric pressure is the weight of the air above us per unit area.
mcqs.explanation: Atmospheric pressure results from the weight of the column of air above a given point, acting over the area of the Earth's surface. Option A states this accurately. Option B confuses atmospheric pressure with tire pressure, which is a separate system. Option C is false because atmospheric pressure exists at all altitudes, decreasing with height. Option D is incorrect because pressure is measured in units such as pascals or atmospheres, not meters.

mcqs.question: Which of the following everyday devices uses fluid pressure to lift a heavy object?

options.A: A lever used to open a door
options.B: A hydraulic jack used to raise a car
options.C: A pulley system used to pull a rope
options.D: A ramp used to move a box

mcqs.answer: A hydraulic jack used to raise a car
mcqs.explanation: A hydraulic jack works on Pascal’s principle: pressure applied to a confined fluid is transmitted equally in all directions, allowing a small force on a small piston to generate a large force on a larger piston. This is a direct application of fluid pressure. The other options rely on mechanical advantage (lever, pulley, ramp) rather than fluid pressure.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the basic idea of pressure
mcqs.question: Two students apply the same force of 100 N on two different surfaces. Student A applies it on a nail tip with an area of 0.5 mm², while Student B applies it on a flat board with an area of 50 cm². Which statement correctly compares the pressures they produce?

options.A: Student A produces a much higher pressure than Student B.
options.B: Student B produces a much higher pressure than Student A.
options.C: Both produce the same pressure because the force is the same.
options.D: Pressure cannot be compared without knowing the material of the surfaces.

mcqs.answer: Student A produces a much higher pressure than Student B.
mcqs.explanation: Pressure = Force / Area. Converting areas: 0.5 mm² = 5 × 10⁻⁷ m²; 50 cm² = 5 × 10⁻³ m². Pressure A = 100 N / 5 × 10⁻⁷ m² = 2 × 10⁸ Pa. Pressure B = 100 N / 5 × 10⁻³ m² = 2 × 10⁴ Pa. Thus, Student A’s pressure is 10,000 times larger. Option A correctly states this; the other options ignore the area difference or introduce irrelevant material considerations.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate pressure to force and area
mcqs.question: A hydraulic press has a small piston of area 2 cm² and a large piston of area 200 cm². If a force of 50 N is applied to the small piston, what is the maximum force that can be lifted by the large piston? (Assume an ideal fluid and neglect friction.)
mcqs.explanation: Pascal’s principle states that pressure is transmitted unchanged: P = F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂. First find the pressure from the small piston: P = 50 N / 2 cm² = 25 N/cm². The large piston area is 200 cm², so the force it can exert is F₂ = P × A₂ = 25 N/cm² × 200 cm² = 5,000 N. Option B matches this calculation; the other options result from incorrect area ratios or omitted conversion.
